span.label: mechanism
span.quote: This article draws theoretical and empirical parallels between them, arguing that they result from a common mechanism, namely, the storage and retrieval of representations of individual exposures to specific items, or instances.

span.label: repetition priming and automaticity
span.quote: Repetition priming and automaticity are both consequences of prior presentations.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: Four experiments were conducted to determine whether repetition priming and automaticity share the three characteristics described above and to determine whether stimulus-to-response or stimulus-to-interpretation associations underlie the effect of multiple repetitions.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: instance theory of automaticity: each encounter with an item stores a memory trace, and with practice performance shifts from a slow general algorithm to fast direct retrieval of stored instances (unifying automaticity and repetition priming)
span.quote: Automatization involves a transition from performance based on a general algorithm to performance based on memory retrieval

span.label: error data were not analyzed because the theories at issue do not address them
span.quote: Since the theories at issue do not address them, error data will not be analysed or presented in detail.

span.label: The transfer effects of Experiment 3 were small and not strongly supported statistically.
span.quote: The effects were relatively small and the statistical support for them was not overwhelmingly strong.

span.label: Alternative learning functions such as exponentials or hyperbolics were never tested against the power-function fits.
span.quote: Second, I have not tried to rule out alternative functions, such as exponentials or hyperbolics, so the fits do not mean that power functions provide the best description of the data.

span.label: The data cannot decide between a declarative and a procedural interpretation of the memory underlying the effect.
span.quote: I prefer the declarative interpretation but I cannot rule out the procedural one.

span.label: Item specificity does not discriminate the instance theory from rival accounts.
span.quote: Item specificity is consistent with the instance theory but it does not uniquely support it.

span.label: a control condition in which subjects saw a NEW set of 10 words and 10 nonwords for the same 16 blocks
span.note: eliminates: that improvement across blocks is general practice at the task rather than item-specific automaticity
span.quote: In the control condition, they saw a new set of 10 words and 10 nonwords for 16 20-trial blocks.

span.label: the assignment of keys to yes and no responses was counterbalanced within each group
span.note: eliminates: that the effect is a motor or hand preference rather than a decision effect
span.quote: The assignment of keys to ‘yes’ and ‘no’ responses was counterbalanced within each group.

span.quote: Theoretically, repetition priming is viewed as the first few steps on the way to automaticity

span.label: automaticity

span.quote: the storage and retrieval of representations of individual exposures to specific items, or instances

span.quote: Does repetition priming increase as a power function of the number of exposures, as speed increases with automatization

span.label: **TWO LITERATURES STUDYING ONE THING AT DIFFERENT DOSES, AND THE DOSE IS WHY THEY NEVER MET:** students of memory investigate `one or two stimulus exposures`; students of attention investigate `several hundred`. Memory calls it repetition priming; attention calls it automaticity. `Theoretically, REPETITION PRIMING IS VIEWED AS THE FIRST FEW STEPS ON THE WAY TO AUTOMATICITY.` **The fourth record today about one name covering two things - and the first running the other way**: forster-davis1984, tulving1990 and was2019 each SPLIT a term the field used as one, and Logan JOINS two the field used as separate
span.quote: Theoretically, repetition priming is viewed as the first few steps on the way to automaticity

span.label: **AND THE CLAIM IS MADE FALSIFIABLE BEFORE IT IS TESTED, BY NAMING THREE PROPERTIES THAT WOULD HAVE TO MATCH:** `The main empirical question asked in this article is whether automaticity and repetition priming share three characteristics: (1) POWER-FUNCTION SPEED-UP ... (2) ITEM SPECIFICITY ... (3) ASSOCIATIVE BASIS.` Each is then phrased as a question - `Does repetition priming increase as a power function of the number of exposures, as speed increases with automatization?` **Three named tests, stated before the experiments, any one of which could have killed the claim.** Same discipline as Schmidt2009's rapid-chase criteria (Q-811), and rare enough in this corpus to be worth counting
span.quote: The main empirical question asked in this article is whether automaticity and repetition priming share three characteristics: (1) Power-Function Speed-Up. Does repetition priming increase as a power function of the number of exposures, as speed increases with automatization

span.label: **AND THE MECHANISM IS A STORAGE CLAIM, WHICH IS WHY ITEM-SPECIFICITY IS A PREDICTION AND NOT A FINDING:** the common mechanism is `the storage and retrieval of representations of INDIVIDUAL EXPOSURES to specific items, OR INSTANCES.` If what is stored is a record of each encounter with a particular item, then benefit MUST be specific to that item - the second characteristic falls out of the theory rather than being observed alongside it. **A theory that predicts one of its own tests is stronger than one that accommodates it**
span.quote: the storage and retrieval of representations of individual exposures to specific items, or instances

span.label: **AND THE BRIDGE IS THE POINT, STATED AS THE ARTICLE'S PURPOSE:** `The purpose of this article is to BEGIN TO BRIDGE THE GAP between the areas by exploring empirical parallels between repetition priming and automaticity and by presenting a theory that integrates them.` **A paper whose contribution is a connection rather than a result** - and for this corpus that is the interesting kind, because a citation graph shows that two literatures do not cite each other and cannot show that they should
span.quote: The purpose of this article is to begin to bridge the gap between the areas by exploring empirical parallels between repetition priming and automaticity and by presenting a theory that integrates them

span.label: contradicts → stimulus-to-response association accounts of automaticity
span.quote: The results provide no evidence that stimulus-to-response associations provide an important basis for automaticity or repetition priming.

span.label: extends → instance theory (Logan, 1988)
span.quote: The results supported the predictions of instance theory and suggested that stimulus-to-interpretation associations underlie the effects.

span.label: contradicts → Morton's (1969, 1979) logogen model and Balota and Chumbley's (1984) familiarity model
span.note: differs in: THE PAPER MARKS THE PARAMETER WITH `IN THAT`. The span: 'The instance theory DIFFERS FROM the logogen model (Morton, 1969, 1979) and the familiarity model (Balota & Chumbley, 1984) IN THAT IT PREDICTS AN ASSOCIATIVE BASIS FOR REPETITION PRIMING AND AUTOMATICITY WHEREAS THOSE MODELS DO N[OT].' The disagreement turns on whether repetition priming has an associative basis - stated, quotable, and absent from the edge until now. Q-437.
span.quote: The instance theory differs from the logogen model (Morton, 1969, 1979) and the familiarity model (Balota & Chumbley, 1984) in that it predicts an associative basis for repetition priming and automaticity whereas those models do not.

span.label: builds-on → the instance theory of automaticity developed in Logan (1988)
span.quote: To show that automaticity and repetition priming share these three characteristics is to show that they can be accounted for by the same theory, the instance theory of automaticity.

span.label: extends → earlier multiple-repetition studies in the lexical decision task (Forbach, Stanners & Hochhaus, 1974; Scarborough et al., 1977; Logan, 1988)
span.quote: The present experiments examined the effects of multiple repetitions in the lexical decision task and fitted power functions to the data to confirm and extend these findings.

span.label: repetition priming —part-of→ automaticity
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — **`THE FIRST FEW STEPS ON THE WAY TO` IS A CONTINUUM CLAIM AND `part-of` IS THE CLOSEST THE VOCABULARY COMES.** It is not that priming is a component of automaticity - it is the same process earlier on. `same-as` would overstate (they differ in degree and in everything that follows from degree); `is-a` is wrong; **there is no `earlier-stage-of` and this is the fifth thing today the enforced vocabulary cannot say** (Q-804, Q-806, Q-812, Q-822). Weight 0.9 and `Theoretically` is inside the quote - this is the article's thesis, and the three characteristics are the test of it.
span.quote: Theoretically, repetition priming is viewed as the first few steps on the way to automaticity
